Pléneau Island lies northeast of Hovgaard Island off the coast of Graham Land. Its low, rocky shores are surrounded by cold Antarctic waters. In this part of the journey, sea ice and icebergs often determine the route available to the ship and boats.

The island is named after Paul Pléneau, a photographer on the French Antarctic Expedition. This area was initially thought to be part of a neighbouring island, but cartographers later identified a narrow passage separating them. Visits to the island and its surrounding waters depend on ice conditions.

A national park has been established around Poás Volcano in Costa Rica. Its main natural attraction is the crater with sulphurous fumaroles. The volcanic landscape offers a glimpse of the processes that continue to shape the Earth's surface and reveals mountain terrain that differs markedly from the lowland tropical rainforest.

The road to Poás passes through rural areas with coffee plantations, flower greenhouses and strawberry farms. As you climb, both the temperature and the vegetation change. This combination of volcanic scenery and farmland makes the journey rewarding even before you reach the main viewpoint. A visit to Poás is often combined with a stop at Doka Coffee Estate and La Paz Waterfalls.

Routes from Cuiabá to the Northern Pantanal pass through Poconé. Beyond the town begins the Transpantaneira, a road that takes travellers onward to nature lodges.

The journey continues with stops to observe wildlife, birds and vegetation. On these itineraries, Poconé connects the urban stretch of the road with the waterways and natural landscapes of the Pantanal.
